summary:
The Maternal and Child Health Stillbirth Prevention Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-69, enacted July 12, 2024, originating as H.R. 4581), amends title V of the Social Security Act to clarify that funds under the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) Services Block Grant may be expended on stillbirth prevention and related outcome research. The Act is a two-provision statute effecting narrow, clarifying amendments; it does not itself appropriate funds or alter the block grant's existing authorization levels.

Section 1 provides the short title and directs that the Act be noted at 42 U.S.C. 1305.

Section 2 amends Section 501(a) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 701(a)), the provision stating the purposes for which the MCH block grant is authorized to be appropriated. Two conforming insertions are made:

First, paragraph (1)(B)—which enumerates purposes relating to reducing infant mortality and the incidence of preventable conditions among children—is amended by inserting "to reduce the incidence of stillbirth," after "among children." This adds stillbirth reduction to the enumerated statutory objectives of the grant program.

Second, paragraph (2) is amended by inserting, after "follow-up services," authorizing language for "evidence-based programs and activities and outcome research to reduce the incidence of stillbirth." The insertion contains a non-exhaustive parenthetical enumeration of permissible activities: tracking and awareness of fetal movements; improvement of birth timing for pregnancies with risk factors; initiatives encouraging safe sleeping positions during pregnancy; screening and surveillance for fetal growth restriction; smoking cessation efforts during pregnancy; community-based home-visiting and support programs; and a residual catch-all for "any other research or evidence-based programming to prevent stillbirths."

The operative mechanism is thus a clarification of permissible use of existing MCH block grant funds rather than the creation of a new grant program, a distinct authorization of appropriations, or any appropriation. The amendments enlarge the statutorily recognized purposes for which States may expend block grant allotments and confirm that stillbirth prevention activities and associated outcome research fall within those purposes.

The Act contains no separate effective-date provision; accordingly, the amendments take effect upon enactment (July 12, 2024). No sunset, deadline, condition precedent, or repeal is specified. The legislative history reflects passage by the House on May 14–15, 2024, and by the Senate on June 11, 2024; House Report No. 118-490 accompanied the bill from the Committee on Energy and Commerce. A companion measure, S. 2231, is noted.
